changelog: Trailers can now come from more than one place. Until now TMDB was the only source, and a title TMDB had no video for simply had no trailer. There are now four sources, tried in an order you control from the Observatory's new Trailers settings group: tmdb (TMDB's videos, language-aware, as before), jellyfin (the trailer URLs Jellyfin's own metadata providers already found for a library item - free, no API key, and already on disk), stored (the URL saved on the catalog row), and search (ask yt-dlp to search YouTube by title and year). Removing a source from the list disables it; reordering changes preference. Search is off by default on purpose, because a text search can return a fan edit or a review and a confidently wrong trailer is worse than none. Three new controls decide which videos are acceptable at all: whether a teaser may stand in when no full trailer exists, whether only videos TMDB marks official are eligible, and whether non-YouTube videos such as Vimeo may be used - each narrows the field without changing the preference order, which still puts a trailer in your language above an official badge. The Trailer Resolver page gains a breakdown of which source actually answered and which were asked and came back empty, so a missing trailer now shows where the search stopped. Note this covers trailer URLs specifically; artwork and overviews still come from TMDB and Jellyfin alone.
